title: Script-first fast path for compose-draft, repair and final compose
targetBucket: critical-chain time of compose-draft, repair, compose (agent turns that only run a deterministic helper or copy files)

baseline.evidence: repair was a no-op in 6/7 runs yet cost an agent turn; repair+final compose on chain 11.7-17.0 s when the draft was clean (median 12.2 s); compose agents spend 64 % of their wall in model calls only to run the helper

change: preflight scripts run first in the same isolate: compose-kernel.mjs --preflight (accept when the parts compile) and repair-noop.mjs (accept when failures.json is empty); the agent runs only when the preflight misses

prediction.perRun: compose-draft + repair + compose on-chain time drops from about 18 s to under 3 s when the draft is clean
prediction.medianWall: drops by at least 12 s (paired by request)

test: fanout-04: the five latest atomizations (C-005 v2, C-007, C-010 v2, C-015, CC-002), same pool shape (5 runs x 4), compared by request with fanout-02/03; mechanism check from preflight.end events
label: Proposed

quality.note: C-010's draft failed one test (a date-anchor expectation) that its run-3 draft passed; the model repair ran and kept the kernel, so this is run-to-run variance in the generated parts, not the fast path, which did not touch that request's repair

title: Router cutover between direct and atomized execution
question: for which requests does the direct single worker reach a promotable artefact sooner than atomize+DAG, end to end including planning
cases: 8: five development singles (tiny to medium) and three constructed large requests stated as single goals (N1 charge diagnosis, N2 ammonia recirculation sizing, N3 supermarket rack commissioning); no pre-decomposed specification

arms.direct: one Sonnet worker, loop-0 protocol, one isolate, same gates
arms.atomized: Sonnet atomizer in an isolate, then the DAG (concurrency 6, script-first fast path, repair stage, reviews)

metric: primary: time to a promotable gated artefact (direct: worker wall; atomized: planning + compose end); secondary: end-to-end including reviews, output tokens, promotable rate

prediction.singles: direct faster on all five (P=0.85), because planning (~45 s) exceeds the parallel saving at 2-7 exports
prediction.N3: atomized faster if both promote (P=0.55); P(direct promotable on N3)=0.6
prediction.cutover: between the largest single and N1

replication: rep 1 for all cases; rep 2 for cases within 25 % of each other
label: Proposed
Recorded (probe)
findings: direct reached a promotable artefact first on all 7 cases where any arm promoted; no cutover inside the ladder, including the three large single-goal requests

direct: promotable 7/8 (S3 failed 14/15 tests); atomized: promotable 5/8 (S3 a test atom returned no output twice; S4 a kernel atom ran 601 s and the draft compose then failed to compile; N2 one blind test expectation was wrong by hand arithmetic and stayed frozen)
atomized used 3-12x the output tokens (S4 145k from a runaway kernel atom)

scope is not equal: on N1 both built six exports; on N3 the direct worker reduced the request to a generic band check (3 exports) while the atomized plan built domain checks (4 exports); atomized wrote 2-5x more tests (N1 124 vs 47) - gates alone cannot compare usefulness

planning alone (47-107 s) exceeds the whole direct run on every case; on N1 the DAG alone (90 s to gated) beat direct (112 s), so with near-zero planning the cutover would sit around N1's size (~15k direct output tokens); on N2 the DAG alone (153 s) lost even without planning

predictionCheck.singles direct faster: met (4/4 where both promoted or direct alone)
predictionCheck.N3: not met; direct promotable and faster
predictionCheck.cutover between largest single and N1: not met as stated; cutover lies beyond N1 at current planning cost

replication: none needed under the precommit rule (no case within 25 %)
next: S-07 direct-first routing by default; atomize only when predicted direct output exceeds a threshold and planning is templated
S-08 template planning (target < 10 s) then re-run N1/N2
S-09 robustness: empty-output guard and per-atom wall cap (S4 601 s), compile-collision repair, blind-test arithmetic check before freezing
quality comparison by the sealed oracle panel on the same artefacts (scope, coverage, usefulness), since speed alone favours the arm that does less

planningSmoke.rejected: env MAX_THINKING_TOKENS ignored; Haiku 13-17 s (thinks more); Codex minimal broke the format, low 26-34 s

prediction.N2: templated faster in at least 2 of 3 (P=0.5); median <= 70 s against direct about 75 s

title: Blind-test expectation check before freezing
baseline: R-02: templated promotable 3/6; every miss was one or two frozen tests with a wrong hand-computed expectation (22/24, 35/36, 23/24)
change: per module: strip (script) removes expected values; check (Sonnet, low effort, tools) computes each case independently with its own code from the need and interface; merge (script) keeps agreeing tests, drops disagreeing ones, widens tol on near-agreement, logs every decision; compose freezes only the merged tests

prediction.templatedMedianGatedS: N1 <= 50 s, N2 <= 70 s (check runs in parallel with the kernel atoms; P=0.6)

test: cutover-03: N1, N2 x 3 reps, arms direct and templated, paired and concurrent
label: Proposed

corrects: finding 3 (every templated failure was a wrong blind-test expectation)
correction: true for N1 r2 only (R-410A at 418 psig expected 110 F; correct is about 120 F). In N2 r1 and r3 the failing test was arithmetically right (100 C = 212 F) but expected a value for an input the interface declares refused (temperatures above 50/60 C); the kernel was right to refuse. Two of three failures were tests contradicting the interface's refusal rule, not arithmetic errors.
evidence: tools/atomizer/work/s09-replay (archived in this commit's ledger notes); repair notes of both N2 runs

run: cutover-03 (N1, N2 x 3, paired) + replay on the three R-02 failures
label: Recorded (probe)

mechanism.replay: N1 r2: both wrong expectations dropped (checker 119.9 F vs test 110 F); N2 r1, r3: missed - the checker computed 212 like the test writer and did not apply the refusal class; a refusal-first instruction in the checker prompt was tried and still missed both

verdict: prediction 'templated promotable >= 5/6' met, but not because of the check: it changed no test in the live run, so the 3/6 -> 6/6 change is unattributed (within chance at n = 6). The check catches arithmetic and property errors (2/2 in replay) and misses tests that contradict the interface's refusal rule (0/2): the checker shares the test writer's blind spot. Kept on (cost about 8 s, catches a real class).
next: S-10 machine-readable refusals: the planner writes refusal ranges per argument (R name.arg lo..hi or codes); a script drops or flips any test that expects a value inside a refused range, before freezing; zero model tokens
replicate cutover-03 to attribute the promotable change
